signals.source_text: Cross-country autonomous flight. From the lakes of Salt Lake City to the hills of North Carolina. Across the plains of Texas… I’ll stop there to spare the butchering of an A++ song, but we’re super excited to showcase our autonomous aircraft, the J208, across the United States starting TODAY! We’ll be flying from our home base in California all the way across the country to where flight itself first took flight, in the Outer Banks of North Carolina, and back again. This is something I’ve been looking forward to doing for the past 5 years working on this aircraft and I’m so excited that it’s finally here and we’re able to showcase the incredible work that this team has put into developing what we believe is one of the most advanced gate-to-gate autonomous systems flying today!

signals.source_text: Robotics beginners unite! 😎 Here's a free course on the basics of robotics, including sensors and autonomous mobile bots. Everyone who studied robotics or EE knows MATLAB and Simulink for Startups very well. I've been using it for designing motors and robots back in the day. MathWorks created a 17-video playlist teaching robotics using real robotic platforms, and other educational kits. Learn how to design, simulate, and control robots. They cover robot navigation with encoders, obstacle detection with IR sensors, vision-based autonomy, smart motor fine-tuning, virtual world simulation, and even modeling wheel-legged robots. Very good for someone just getting started and looking for a low entry-point course totally for free. Simulink modeling for control, Stateflow for state machines, hardware support packages, external mode debugging, virtual simulation before physical deployment. You can actually work on real robotics platforms! This is how you start in robotics! 🔗 Free YouTube vid library: https://lnkd.in/edtzzrFu ~~ ♻️ Join the weekly robotics newsletter, and never miss any news → ziegler.substack.com

signals.source_text: The EV didn't make NVH easier. It pushed the noise higher. Motor whine past 5 kHz. Gear mesh. Inverter harmonics. Road noise now the loudest source in the cabin. The critical band runs 100 Hz to 5 kHz, and no single method covers it. The Engineer's Guide to Modern NVH Simulation shows how to work the full range in MSC Nastran and Actran: heavy-fluid coupling, Virtual SEA, and ODYSSEE ROMs. Preview the first pages, then download the full guide below 👇

signals.source_text: Back in California for week two of training with Joby Aviation , and while looking through some of the cards we share at workforce events, one message immediately caught my eye: Become a dreamer. Dream big.🌟 I smiled because that message has always resonated with me. I’ve spent much of my career encouraging others to see what’s possible, pursue new opportunities, and take meaningful steps toward their goals. I also know firsthand that dreams can change, evolve, and sometimes lead us in directions we never expected. That’s one of the things I appreciate about workforce development: helping people imagine new possibilities for themselves and connect those possibilities to real career pathways. I’m grateful to be learning alongside people who think boldly about the future and who believe big ideas are worth pursuing. Sometimes a simple card can say a lot.
